discrepancies_and_observations.observation: premiumIndexKlines CLOSE intermittently emits exact 0.0 when the premium index did not update at the bucket boundary (verified against raw rows: open/high/low carry real values, close is 0; volume fields 0; mark klines carry forward, premium klines do not). Sentinel shares over the authorized window: ACE 48.5%, ONG 48.1%, BOME 30.7%, ZEC 29.1%, NEAR 14.3%, ENA 13.5%, WLD 10.7%, LINK 8.1%, BCH 6.9%, ADA 6.0%, AAVE 5.4%, AVAX 5.4%, 1000PEPE 3.9%, BNB 2.7%, SUI 2.4%, DOGE 1.8%, XRP 1.7%, SOL 0.6%, ETH 0.1%. Under the proposals' frozen fail-closed rule (L-V12-5: malformed == missing; no back-fill, no synthesis), PREMVOL's 2880-slot clean window is unreachable: only 3/19 symbols (BNB, XRP, ETH) have even ONE fully-clean 2880-bucket window anywhere in the authorized window, and the panel measures ZERO eligible names at essentially every stamp (min_iqr=0). Its 90d neighbour is strictly worse. PREMREV's 31-value footprint survives on a shrunken universe: eligible counts min 4 / median 8 (vs the 19-name design), meeting its own N >= 4 floor at every stamp. Verdict routing per the proposals' own failure tables: PREMVOL -> BLOCKED_DATA ('premium-kline coverage gaps force N < 4 persistently - data problem, not economics'); PREMREV -> feasible with drastically reduced breadth (A1 should weigh whether the reduced-universe reading still matches the design intent before selection).

/futures/data/basis futuresPrice is the perp's LAST-TRADED price while markPriceKlines close is the MARK price, so PREMFADE's p_b and WIDTHGATE's m_b are different premium bases by construction (route-specific and self-consistent within each proposal). Measured BTCUSDT 2024-08-20T00:00Z: basis-route futuresPrice 59398.40 vs mark close 59368.34.

The mark/index-derived premium and the endpoint premium kline are distinct observables whose disagreement grows with illiquidity: measured abs-deviation medians ~5e-5 (SOL) to ~6.5e-4 (ONG), per-symbol MAXima 8.7e-2 (ONG), 4.5e-2 (ACE), 2.0e-2 (SOL), 1.7e-2 (ZEC/WLD), 1.7e-2 (ENA) -- all recorded per symbol in the WIDTHGATE panel's staging_identity_check block. A fixed tight band (1e-3) fails several names; a 1e-1 band is trivially loose. A1/I-lane must declare the tolerance from this measured table (or accept the per-symbol fail-closed drops it implies); the WIDTHGATE route data itself is complete (19/19 names x 70,272 buckets).

discrepancies_and_observations.observation: premiumIndexKlines close is NOT exactly markClose/indexClose-1 per bucket (Binance derives the premium kline from higher-frequency snapshots). Measured abs deviation: mean ~4.0e-5, max ~4.2e-4 (BTCUSDT 500-bucket sample). The proposal's 'declared relative tolerance' must be an ABSOLUTE band (~1e-3) or it will flag near-zero-premium buckets spuriously; the lane's panel declares tolerance_abs=1e-3 and records per-symbol maxima.

52 Monday stamps exist in the blind-S0 window; the frozen 1-day fold purge removes the 2025-12-22 stamp, leaving 51 live stamps per arm. A6's >= 48 floor passes; A5's and A8's text floors of '52 weekly decisions' are met only by the SCHEDULED calendar. A1 should record which reading binds at selection; no data failure involved.

'trailing 30d standard deviation of consecutive 72h premium changes' is ambiguous between daily-sampled (30 changes) and every-15m-overlapping (~2880 changes) readings. The lane's panel uses the DAILY-SAMPLED reading (declared in the artifact); the 72h-change numerator and rank ordering are identical under both, only the sigma scale differs.

The endpoint intermittently returns HTTP 418 with an empty body under serial ~0.55-0.9s pacing (29/76 first-pass point anchors, 14/76 retries; kline routes never returned 418 in the same runs). The I-lane staging for PREMFADE MUST implement 418 backoff-retry (this lane's stager uses up to 8 attempts with linear 20s backoff). Full-window staging completed with ZERO missing buckets on all routes, so the data are retrievable; the quirk is operational.

The day's last 5m OI metrics snapshot lands before 23:55Z on 48-59 of 417 days per symbol (documented in OICH section 4). Calendar-day completeness is 417/417 with zero missing/duplicate day rows; consecutive-ness by day-row index as the proposals freeze. Not a gap.

Under the remediated kernel with real ticks, the diversified upper-bound fill arithmetic gives ~6.5% base / ~11.8% stressed annual drag of gross (inside the 8%/12% floors, stress marginal), while the pathological all-fills-on-the-worst-tick-name bound (NEARUSDT) gives 10.9%/24.9% (breach). The MEASURED schedules reconstructed from the frozen rank rules churn far less than the bounds and pass both floors with wide margin for every measurable proposal (see per-proposal measured_turnover_schedule_only); the no-symbol->25%-of-turnover floor also passes everywhere measured (max 13.3%).
